Apparently there was no guarantee of a minimum compensation, because it is equally clear that either one would be accepted as his successor. In other cases the interest would be passed back to Mr. Halsell or other owners upon the retirement of a holder. Unfortunately, as most of these deeds were never filed for record, the complete financial story is not available, nevertheless the general pattern of ownership has been thus established. On June 22, 1883, by a deed dated June 22, 1883, Mr. Halsell and R. B. Holland purchased a big interest in the College from Professor Priechett; by which B. R. Halsell alone sold to the addition of Professor Priechett: by the College of the same year, by which B. R. Halsell alone sold to E. F. Montgomery a quarter interest in the "College and land," and which is understandable only on the conjecture that intervening deeds were lost. It seems most reasonable to suggest that with the addition of a fourth professor to the operating faculty the interest of a fourth share was considered necessary. This supposition seems to be further warranted by the statement of Mr. W. I. Hunt that he, as one of the four college teachers in 1887-1888, owned a one-fourth interest.

The Personnel and Training of the Faculty.—After the admission of two faculty members with Mr. President Halsell and Holland in 1883, the number of men on the strictly Collegiate faculty increased to four.
